description.reference: List all runs for a workflow execution
description.candidate: List a page of runs for a workflow execution

help.reference:
List every run (including retries and continue-as-new successors) for a
workflow ID, oldest first.

<comment>Examples:</comment>

  <info>dw workflow:list-runs chk-42</info>
  <info>dw workflow:list-runs chk-42 --json</info>
help.candidate:
Return one Server response page for a workflow ID, in the Server's order.
This command sends one request and does not follow next_page_token.
JSON keeps the response envelope and any cursor; JSONL emits only the
returned run records. The page may include retries and continue-as-new
successors. Use --json to inspect whether the Server returned a cursor.

<comment>Examples:</comment>

  <info>dw workflow:list-runs chk-42</info>
  <info>dw workflow:list-runs chk-42 --json</info>

help.reference:
Deliver an asynchronous signal to a running workflow. The signal is
durably recorded in history even if the workflow is currently idle or
waiting.

<comment>Examples:</comment>

  <info>dw workflow:signal chk-42 approve</info>
  <info>dw workflow:signal chk-42 payment_received -i '{"amount":99.95}'</info>
help.candidate:
Deliver an asynchronous signal to a running workflow. The signal is
durably recorded in history even if the workflow is currently idle or
waiting.

Every signal carries a caller command key (<comment>request_id</comment>).
The CLI generates one per invocation unless <comment>--request-id</comment>
is given, and prints the key it used. An explicit empty or whitespace-only
key is refused. After a lost response the outcome is unknown: inspect
workflow history and command receipts before retrying. A request ID alone
does not prove that a repeated signal is safe. Rely on retained admission
and intent-conflict guarantees only when the Server advertises that
capability; legacy servers may store a key without deduplicating signals.

<comment>Examples:</comment>

  <info>dw workflow:signal chk-42 approve</info>
  <info>dw workflow:signal chk-42 payment_received -i '{"amount":99.95}'</info>
  <info>dw workflow:signal chk-42 approve --request-id=approve-chk-42-2026-10-20 --json</info>

description.reference: Serve an existing Laravel project for local development
description.candidate: Start the built-in native development Server

help.reference:
Run this command from an installed, configured Laravel project's directory.
An external PHP executable is required, even when using the native dw binary.
This launches Artisan's HTTP server. Configure the database and run migrations
first, and run the project's queue worker and scheduler separately when needed.
Restart this command after editing the project's .env configuration.

SQLite is the default database driver. For <comment>mysql</comment> or
<comment>pgsql</comment>, your project's Docker Compose configuration must
define that service and <comment>redis</comment>. Dependencies are left running
when the HTTP process stops. The bind address defaults to loopback.

For a standalone Durable Workflow Server, follow the Docker-backed quickstart:
https://durable-workflow.com/docs/quickstart/

<comment>Examples:</comment>

  <info>dw server:start-dev</info>
  <info>dw server:start-dev --port=9000</info>
  <info>dw server:start-dev --db=mysql</info>
help.candidate:
Start a local Durable Workflow Server using the native runtime and SQLite
compiled into dw. Run it from any directory. No PHP, Docker, Redis, separate
Server installation or runtime download is needed. The runtime creates its
schema and default namespace and runs its own timers and maintenance.

The address defaults to 127.0.0.1:8080 and only loopback binds are accepted.
Use --port=0 to choose an available port. Data persists under dw's config
folder in dev-server, or the directory selected with --data-dir. Only one
Server may use a data directory at a time. Ctrl+C closes the runtime and keeps
the data. SDK workers still run your application code separately.

The local development token is dev-token. Set --token to choose another.
Existing native DW_* payload, query and storage limits also apply. This is
a CLI-linked development build. Its source is pinned in the CLI dependency lock.

<comment>Examples:</comment>

  <info>dw server:start-dev</info>
  <info>dw server:start-dev --port=9000 --data-dir=./workflow-data</info>

  # In another terminal, connect the CLI to the local Server
  <info>dw env:set local --server=http://127.0.0.1:8080 --token=dev-token --make-default</info>
  <info>dw doctor</info>
